newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Auditor tells Czech Agrobanka to double reserves.
newsitem.headline: Auditor tells Czech Agrobanka to double reserves.

text.p: International auditor Price Waterhouse has told troubled Czech bank Agrobanka a.s. it needs to double its reserves to some 10 billion crowns, a bank official said on Tuesday.
"The (preliminary) audit shows the need for reserves to be raised by about two times their level in September (five billion crowns)," Agrobanka spokesman Milan Srb told Reuters.
He added that a final audit of the bank's books should be completed in one or two months.
In September, Agrobanka, the fifth largest bank, went into forced administration because of low liquidity connected to the failure of a smaller Plzen-based bank, Kreditni Banka a.s..
The central bank is currently searching for a majority shareholder to take control of Agrobanka which was connected to Kreditni through an obscure investment firm called Motoinvest.
The failure of Kreditni, which investigators said was caused by dubious debt- swap deals linked to Motoinvest, in turn caused a crisis in confidence in Agrobanka.

Agrobanka was the 12th and so far the largest Czech bank to have been subjected to central bank intervention, since post-Communist liberalisation of the sector created dozens of new banks in the early 1990s.
But the central bank stresses that more than 70 percent of banking activity in the country is conducted with the so-called "Big Four" banks.
